name: TOGAF EPIC v3 - recursive index-planned, reference-grounded SAD
description: Contract for the v3 depth layer executed by scripts/togaf_epic_v3.py. Stands on the v2 pipeline (evidence pack, diagrams-as-code, PDF SVG gate) and adds: a TOGAF-prescribed skeleton as a deterministic floor, recursive per-chapter index planning, per-section grounded writing with mandatory citations, an ICONIX robustness model with per-object catalogs, and a resumable state file.
doctrine: The TOGAF skeleton (7 chapters, prescribed artifacts per chapter) is the FLOOR - the planner extends it, never removes from it.
Recursive planning: document index -> chapter index -> leaf sections; each leaf is its own gated LLM call.
Frameworks are prescribed per chapter and enforced per section: SWOT, PESTEL, 5W1H.
Every section writes against a citable evidence bundle and MUST cite [EV-*] labels inline and end with a References block; the gate rejects otherwise, with one named-failure retry.

Robustness model is deterministic: every significant code-graph object classified Boundary/Control/Entity by path heuristics, each object gets a catalog ID (B-nn/C-nn/E-nn) and its own index row; diagram edges are real DEPENDS_ON pairs.
Resumable: state file per output dir; --resume skips written sections; --max-leaves bounds a build.
Same observability as v2: AER events per plan/write/assemble phase, visible at :8788.

chapters.extra: robustness model + per-object catalogs live here

honest_costs: At the measured 3.8 tok/s (eGPU/LAN gemma-4-12b), a full ~50-section build is an overnight run (~4-6h). Use --max-leaves for bounded builds and --resume to continue; sections already written are never re-paid.
